title: Max at the Harvest Festival
author: Shellfie original
credit: An original story written for the McKinley Bulldogs.

pages: The Harvest Festival is the biggest party of the year at McKinley. For two evenings in October, the yards fill with game booths, food, music, and families from all over town. Max has been counting down the days on the kitchen calendar.

First, Max and Grandma buy tickets. Max plays the bean bag toss and wins a tiny plastic pumpkin. At the next booth, Max tries to knock down a tower of cans, but the cans don't budge. "They must be glued," Max jokes. The volunteer laughs. "Try aiming lower." On the next throw, the whole tower crashes down.
Max smells something delicious. There are tacos, popcorn, and cupcakes decorated like spiders. Max picks a spider cupcake and eats it in four bites, leaving frosting on both ears.

Then Max sees a crowd near the stage. It is the Thriller dancers! Max cheers for the fourth and fifth graders as they shuffle and claw their way through the zombie dance. Nearby, grown-ups are looking at the auction table, where families bid on prizes like a pizza party or a day of fun with a teacher.

As the sun goes down, the strings of lights turn on and the yard glows orange. Max sits on a hay bale next to Grandma, full and sleepy. "Why do we have a Harvest Festival?" Max asks. Grandma says, "To celebrate fall, to raise money for the school, and to be together as a community." Max yawns. "I like the together part best."

quiz.q: What did Max win at the bean bag toss?
quiz.ev: Max plays the bean bag toss and wins a tiny plastic pumpkin.

quiz.q: Why did the cans finally fall?
quiz.ev: "Try aiming lower." On the next throw, the whole tower crashes down.

o: A group of people who share a place and care about each other
quiz.ev: to be together as a community
